text: Audit Spending and Deliver Results With a state budget that has doubled in just a decade, Christine knows that government can tighten its belt and return to their core mission of serving people – not their political agendas and special interests. Christine has built a reputation for standing up to entrenched power, challenging waste and mismanagement, and fighting for common-sense solutions that make life more affordable, safer, and more hopeful for Oregon families. ... Break the Cycle of Homelessness and Addiction From tent cities to government funded crack pipes, across Oregon you’ll see the human tragedy that far-left policies have created. Christine will work to ensure that homelessness is rare and temporary, not chronic and permanent. We need fewer needles and more cops to restore safe communities. ... Read More

Lower the Cost of Living From the cost of buying a home to filling up the tank, families across our state cannot afford a government that fails to put them first. Christine knows that Oregon’s affordability crisis didn’t happen by accident. It was created by out-of-touch politicians with hidden agendas that continue to make life more expensive. ... Read More

Reignite Oregon’s Economy High taxes, overregulation and radical politicians are forcing Main Street to close up shop – eliminating thousands of jobs. State agencies are there to serve, not punish. Christine understands that for Oregon to be the best place to start and grow a business, government needs to get out of the way. ... Read More

Restore Graduation Requirements As a mom who’s spent time in the classroom, Christine knows that parents should make decisions about their children’s education. Increasingly parents find their authority undermined, their values dismissed, and their children exposed to radical ideologies at younger and younger ages. ... Read More

Unlock the Door to Homeownership Young families are priced out of homeownership and seniors on fixed incomes face property taxes that force impossible choices. Red tape in Salem, outdated forest management policies, and some of the highest taxes in the nation are keeping you and your family from buying a home. Christine understands that the best thing bureaucrats and politicians can do to lower the cost of housing is get out of the way. ... Read More
